# opencode-gitlab-titler

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) server plugin that names a session after the GitLab merge request or issue in your first message, so you can find the session later by project, number or title.

It works in any project whose git `origin` remote points at a GitLab instance: gitlab.com or a self-managed instance, over ssh or http(s). The plugin reads the remote to learn which instance and project `MR 45` or `#45` mean, so there is nothing to set up per project. Outside a git repository, or where `origin` is not a GitLab project, it uses `gitlab-org/gitlab` on `gitlab.com`. See [Which project and host](#which-project-and-host). You need [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) signed in to each instance you use.

| First message | Session title |
|---|---|
| mentions "review" and names an MR | `Reviewing (gitlab-org/gitlab\|!123) MR title` |
| names an issue (with or without "review", unless it also reviews an MR) | `(gitlab-org/gitlab\|#45) Issue title` |
| no "review", names an MR you wrote | `(gitlab-org/gitlab\|!123) MR title` |
| anything else | OpenCode's own title. Its title model is told the same format, to use when the message clearly names an item |

The MR or issue is fetched with one `glab api` request. It runs inside OpenCode's `title` hook, which fires once per session while the title is generated, so the name is set before any work starts and nothing renames it later.

## Naming an MR or issue

A message can name an MR or issue in three ways. All of them are looked up in GitLab.

| Written as | Means |
|---|---|
| `https://gitlab.com/group/project/-/merge_requests/123`, `/-/issues/45` or `/-/work_items/45` | That item. The project comes from the link. |
| `group/project!123` or `group/project#45` | That item. |
| `!123`, `MR 123`, `merge request 123`, `#45`, `issue 45`, `work item 45` | That number in the project of the repository you are in (below). |

A bare `#45` anywhere in the first message counts, so a message that uses `#3` for something else ("fix step #3") is read as issue 3 in the project of the repository. Say "step 3" to avoid it.

### Which project and host

There is nothing to configure. The plugin reads the `origin` remote of the directory the session is in (`git remote get-url origin`) and uses its host and project. In a clone of `gitlab-org/gitlab`, "review MR 45" and "Investigate #29832" name `gitlab-org/gitlab!45` and `gitlab-org/gitlab#29832`. In a clone of `team/app` on `gitlab.example.com`, the same words name `team/app!45` and `team/app#29832` on that host.

Both kinds of remote work:

| Remote | Host | Project |
|---|---|---|
| `git@gitlab.com:gitlab-org/gitlab.git` | `gitlab.com` | `gitlab-org/gitlab` |
| `ssh://git@gitlab.example.com:2222/team/app.git` | `gitlab.example.com` | `team/app` |
| `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab.git` | `gitlab.com` | `gitlab-org/gitlab` |
| `https://user@gitlab.example.com/group/sub/app` | `gitlab.example.com` | `group/sub/app` |
| `http://gdk.test:3000/root/project.git` | `gdk.test:3000` | `root/project` |

The port of an ssh remote is the ssh port, so it is dropped. The port of an http or https remote is kept. A `.git` ending, a trailing slash and a user or token in the URL are ignored.

When it cannot be worked out, the plugin uses `gitlab-org/gitlab` on `gitlab.com`. That happens when the directory is not a git repository, git has no `origin` yet, or the remote is not a GitLab project path: a local path, an ssh alias with no dot in it that git did not expand, or a remote on `github.com` or `bitbucket.org`. It is read again for every new session and retitle, so adding `origin` later needs no reload.

## Rules

1. The first MR and the first issue in the message are the ones used. A link wins over a `group/project!n` reference, which wins over a bare number. Others are ignored.
2. "review" means the word `review`, `reviews`, `reviewed` or `reviewing`, in any case. `preview` and `code_review` do not count.
3. Review and an MR: always a review title, whoever wrote the MR. This wins even when the message also names an issue.
4. Any issue otherwise: an issue title, even when the message says "review". An issue next to "review" and no MR means you are starting work on it, not reviewing it. The issue also wins over an MR that is not being reviewed.
5. No review, no issue, and an MR: the MR is named only when its author is you. Someone else's MR gets the default title, with no guidance.
6. Anything else, including review with nothing named: the default title, with guidance (below).
7. If GitLab cannot be reached, or `glab` fails, the plugin logs `[gitlab-titler] no GitLab title: <reason>` and falls back to the default title, with guidance. A GitLab problem never blocks a session.

Links are only read when they point at the host of the repository (above). Work items are looked up as issues.

## Guided titles

Sometimes the plugin cannot look an item up: "continue the work from yesterday" names nothing, and a lookup can fail. In those cases the plugin adds a short instruction to OpenCode's own title request. It asks the title model to use the same shapes when one item is clearly identified and clearly being worked on:

- `Reviewing (<project>|!<iid>) <description>` for a merge request being reviewed
- `(<project>|#<iid>) <description>` for an issue, even when the message says review
- `(<project>|!<iid>) <description>` for a merge request being worked on

The model cannot fetch the real title, so it writes the description from your message. It is told to take the project and number from the message, to use the project of the repository for a number with no project, never to invent either, and otherwise to write a normal title. Set `guideTitle` to `false` to turn this off. A title the plugin builds from GitLab never uses the model, so it is never guided.

## The `/gitlab-titler` command

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/gitlab-titler enable` | Turn the plugin on for the current project. |
| `/gitlab-titler disable` | Turn it off for the current project. New sessions get OpenCode's own title, with no guidance. |
| `/gitlab-titler retitle` | Name the current session again, from the whole conversation. |
| `/gitlab-titler update` | Install the newest version of the plugin. |
| `/gitlab-titler` | Open a dialog with the same choices. So does any text it does not understand, after a warning. |

The dialog shows whether the plugin is on and three choices: turn it on or off, "Retitle this session" and "Update plugin". The text under the choices follows the cursor. On the first row it describes what the plugin does. On "Retitle this session" it says retitle reads the whole conversation, not only the first message. On "Update plugin" it says the update comes from npm and reloads the plugin. Move with the arrow keys (or `j` and `k`), choose with Enter, close with Esc. Retitle is greyed out on the home screen. The setting is stored per project, not per session, and survives restarts. The plugin is on until you turn it off. Retitle works whether the plugin is on or off.

### Update

"Update plugin" uses OpenCode's own plugin updater, the same one behind `opencode plugin update`. It checks whether a newer version of this package is on npm, installs it and reloads the plugin in every open session. There is nothing to restart. You get a toast saying what happened: updated, already on the newest version, or why nothing was done.

It does nothing for a plugin loaded from a local directory, or one pinned to a version in `plugins` such as `"opencode-gitlab-titler@1.0.0"`. Remove the version to update.

The command is also in the command palette as "GitLab titler".

### Retitle

The automatic title only ever sees the first message. Retitle looks at the whole session, so it can follow work that has moved on: an issue you picked up later, or an MR you opened.

1. It reads the session's messages: everything you typed, the assistant's prose and any compaction summary. Tool calls, reasoning and shell output are left out. A long session keeps its start and its most recent messages, up to about 12,000 characters, and says how many it dropped.
2. It looks up the real title of the first MR and the first issue you named anywhere in the session, so the title model can reuse them instead of guessing.
3. It sends the transcript, those titles and the same format instructions as the guided title to the title model, and asks for one line.
4. It cleans the answer (quotes, a `Title:` label, a second line), cuts it to `maxTitleLength` and renames the session.

If the model returns nothing usable, the session has no messages, or the model call fails, the title is left alone and you see a toast with the reason.

Which model: the model set for the `title` agent in your OpenCode config, if there is one.

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "title": { "model": "gitlab/duo-chat-haiku-5-5" }
  }
}
```

Without that, the model OpenCode itself last used to title a session, which is its own small-model choice. If no title has been generated since the plugin was installed, OpenCode's default model is used. The plugin reads OpenCode's config on every retitle, so changing `agents.title.model` needs no restart.

## Install

Requirements:

- OpenCode 2.0.9 or newer.
- [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) installed and signed in to every host you use: `glab auth login` (add `--hostname <host>` for a self-managed instance). Check with `glab api user`.

Add the package to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. OpenCode installs it and its dependencies. One entry loads the server part (title hook, on/off setting, retitle) and the terminal part (`/gitlab-titler`):

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-gitlab-titler"]
}
```

Pin a version with `"opencode-gitlab-titler@1.0.0"`. To set options, create `~/.config/opencode/gitlab-titler.config.json` (see [Options](#options)):

```json
{
  "maxTitleLength": 200
}
```

Run `/reload` or start a new session. To check it loaded, type `/gitlab-titler`, or start a new session with an MR link as the first message.

### From a local checkout

Run `bun install` once in the checkout, then point `package` at the directory:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "file:///path/to/opencode-gitlab-titler" }]
}
```

### Uninstall

Remove the entry from `plugins`. The per-project on/off setting stays in OpenCode's plugin storage, and `gitlab-titler.config.json` stays on disk. Neither does anything without the plugin.

## Options

Options live in `~/.config/opencode/gitlab-titler.config.json`, a JSON object (no comments). If `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, the file is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/gitlab-titler.config.json` instead. The file is optional: without it every option has its default.

```json
{
  "maxTitleLength": 200,
  "currentUser": "my-username"
}
```

The file is read once, when the plugin loads. After editing it, run `/reload`.

The project and host are not options. See [Which project and host](#which-project-and-host).

Options in the `plugins` entry of `opencode.jsonc` (`"options": { ... }`) are ignored. The plugin logs a warning if it finds any. Move them into the file.

All options are optional. A value of the wrong type is ignored and the default is used. An option name it does not know is ignored with a warning, which includes `host` and `defaultProject` from older versions. A file that cannot be read, is not valid JSON or is not an object gives the defaults and a warning. A typo or a bad file cannot stop the plugin from loading.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxTitleLength` | `100` | Longest the MR or issue title can be before it is cut with `…`. At least 10. The project and number are never cut. |
| `currentUser` | looked up with `glab api user` | GitLab username that counts as you for MRs without "review". Set it to skip the lookup. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `15` | How long one `glab` call may take. |
| `guideTitle` | `true` | Add the title format to OpenCode's title request when the plugin cannot build a title from what the message names. |

`glab` is found through `$GLAB_PATH`, then `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `~/.local/bin`, then `PATH`, because the OpenCode server may not have Homebrew on its `PATH`.

## Safety

- Read-only: `glab api` is only ever given a path, so it can only send GET. The tests check this.
- `glab` is started with an argument array and no shell, so nothing in a message can be run as a command.
- Links to any host other than the repository's host are never fetched.
- The only other command the plugin runs is `git remote get-url origin`, which reads one setting. It is started with an argument array and no shell, like `glab`.
- Update runs OpenCode's own plugin updater for this one package. It does not touch other plugins.
- The plugin never reads or stores a token. `glab` holds the credentials.
- Retitle sends a trimmed copy of your conversation to the title model. That is the same model that already sees your first message, and it is the only place the plugin sends more than that.

## Troubleshooting

The plugin warns with lines starting `[gitlab-titler]`. They are written by the OpenCode server process, so look in the server log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`) or its output. The messages below follow that prefix.

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `no GitLab title: spawn glab ENOENT` | `glab` is not installed or not in a place the server looks. Install it, or set `GLAB_PATH` in the environment OpenCode starts from. |
| `no GitLab title:` with an authentication error | `glab` is not signed in to that host. Run `glab auth login --hostname <host>`. |
| `could not read`, `is not valid JSON`, `ignoring unknown option` or `ignoring "host"` for `gitlab-titler.config.json` | The config file has a problem, and the defaults are used for what could not be read. Fix the file and run `/reload`. |
| `options in the plugins entry are ignored` | Options now live in `gitlab-titler.config.json`. Move them there and remove `options` from the entry. |
| A setting in `gitlab-titler.config.json` has no effect | The file is read when the plugin loads. Run `/reload`. Check the option name and type in [Options](#options). |
| A link is ignored | Its host is not the host of the repository the session is in. Check `git remote get-url origin` there. |
| `MR 45` or `#45` names the wrong project | Numbers are looked up in the project of the `origin` remote of the session's directory, or `gitlab-org/gitlab` when there is none. Check `git remote get-url origin`, or write `group/project!45`. |
| The session gets OpenCode's own title | The plugin is off for this project (`/gitlab-titler enable`), the message names no MR or issue, or the MR is someone else's and the message does not say "review". |
| "Update plugin" says there is nothing to update | The plugin is loaded from a local directory, or pinned to a version in `plugins`. |
| `/gitlab-titler` is missing | The terminal part did not load. Run `/reload` and check the entry in `opencode.jsonc` and your OpenCode version. |

## Development

OpenCode reloads a plugin every time one of its files is saved, in every open session. Do not edit this plugin while it is listed in your OpenCode config. Remove it from `plugins`, edit and test, then add it back.

```sh
bun install
bun test              # unit tests
bun run test:render   # draws the dialog in a headless OpenTUI renderer
bun run typecheck
```

`bun run test` runs both test commands. The tests never touch the network or a running OpenCode. The render check is a script, not a `bun test` file, because `bun test` loads two copies of Solid next to OpenTUI, which breaks reactivity.

The render check runs twice. `test:render:solid` preloads the Solid compiler, which is how OpenCode loads a plugin from a `file://` checkout. `test:render:static` does not (it uses `test/bunfig.static.toml`), which is how OpenCode loads a plugin installed from npm, because it lives under `node_modules`. JSX is not reactive on that path. The dialog therefore keeps its cursor in a plain variable and repaints the rows itself instead of using Solid signals. Keep it that way: a signal from the plugin's own copy of `solid-js` moved the cursor but never repainted the screen, and only the static run catches that.

| File | Does |
|---|---|
| `src/refs.ts` | Finds the MR and issue a message names (links, `group/project!n`, bare numbers) and decides which one names the session. |
| `src/title.ts` | Builds the title string and cuts it to length. |
| `src/options.ts`, `src/config.ts` | The options and their defaults, and reading them from `gitlab-titler.config.json`. |
| `src/origin.ts` | Works out the host and project from the git `origin` remote (http and ssh). Runs `git remote get-url origin`. |
| `src/gitlab.ts` | Talks to `glab`, which it starts in `glabRunner`. |
| `src/resolve.ts` | Turns a message into a title, "leave it alone", or "guide the model". |
| `src/guidance.ts` | The format instructions added to the title request. |
| `src/hook.ts` | The `title` hook body: on/off, then resolve, then set the title or add guidance. |
| `src/state.ts` | The per-project on/off setting and the remembered title model. |
| `src/transcript.ts`, `src/retitle.ts` | Retitle: render the session, build the prompt, call the model, rename. |
| `src/service.ts`, `src/rpc.ts` | The server side of `/gitlab-titler` and its RPC contract. |
| `src/command.ts`, `src/menu.ts`, `src/update.ts` | The slash command: logic, dialog cursor movement, and the plugin update. |
| `src/dialog.tsx`, `src/tui.ts` | The dialog (OpenTUI and Solid, loaded on demand), and the terminal wiring. If the dialog cannot load, the command falls back to OpenCode's plain select dialog. |
| `src/index.ts` | The server part: wires everything to OpenCode. |

### Testing against a real server

Unit tests cover the logic. To exercise the title hook, the RPC and retitle against a real OpenCode, use a plugin lab (the author's is `opencode-plugin-lab`, not part of this package). It starts a private server with its own database and a mock model, so it cannot reach your sessions or the shared service. The checks that matter: titles for an issue link, a review, a review with only an issue link, a bare `MR 45`, and no reference at all; the guidance reaching the title request; `setEnabled` switching the hook off and on; `retitle` renaming a session and failing cleanly on an empty one; one `loading plugin` line per location; no errors in the server log.

The terminal part (`src/tui.ts`) needs a real TUI, run from the npm install layout (a copy under a `node_modules` directory), not only from a checkout, because the two load JSX differently. A pty-driven TUI against the private server works: type `/gitlab-titler`, send Down, and read which row the `▸` is on. Its logic is in `src/command.ts`, `src/menu.ts` and `src/update.ts` and is unit tested, and the dialog's drawing and keys are covered by the render check. Only the wiring to OpenCode's client, toasts and dialog host is not.

## Publishing

```sh
bun install
npm version <patch|minor|major>
npm publish   # runs typecheck and tests first (prepublishOnly)
```

`npm pack --dry-run` should list only `src/`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `package.json`. The package ships TypeScript source, which OpenCode runs directly, so there is no build step.
